faq.a: A neuron is a nerve cell that carries messages as tiny electrical and chemical signals. Your brain has about 86 billion of them, linked in a huge network.
asks: How many neurons are in the brain?

faq.q: How does a signal start in the brain?
faq.a: Your senses, like your eyes, turn what you see or hear into electrical signals that travel along neurons into the brain.
asks: Tell me about see the note
How does the eye send messages?

faq.q: Why do links between neurons get stronger?
faq.a: When neurons send signals to each other again and again, the connection between them, called a synapse, grows stronger and faster. People say neurons that fire together wire together.
asks: What does fire together wire together mean?

faq.q: Why does practice make things easier?
faq.a: Practice strengthens the brain paths used for a skill, so signals travel faster and more smoothly, and you need less effort and thought.
Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change and make new connections when you learn and practise. It happens at every age, though it is especially strong in children.

facts: A 2009 study by Suzana Herculano-Houzel estimated the human brain has about 86 billion neurons.
The idea that "cells that fire together wire together" comes from psychologist Donald Hebb's 1949 theory of learning.
